title: Ann Arbor Farmers Market Saturday Market Regular Hours
Trick or Treat on the River
description:
Help create one of Ann Arbor Parks’ most unique fall traditions!
On Sunday, October 11, families will paddle around Gallup Pond on the Huron River, stopping at themed stations to collect treats from costumed volunteers. Whether you greet paddlers from the shoreline, help with activities on land, or provide flexible event support, you’ll help create a memorable Halloween adventure for children and families.
The public event runs from 12:00–4:00 p.m.
Choose Your Shift
Early Shift: 11:30 a.m.–2:30 p.m.
Help welcome the first paddlers and support the first half of the event.
Afternoon Shift: 2:00–5:00 p.m.
Support the second half of the event and help pack up your station, activity area, or supplies when the event ends.
Want to volunteer longer? You’re encouraged to sign up for both shifts at the same station.
What to Expect
Most volunteers will walk from check-in to their assigned station or activity area and will stand for much of their shift. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring a reusable water bottle.
Costumes, volunteer shirts, and necessary equipment will be provided based on your assignment. Some roles have additional physical or safety requirements, which will be explained in the individual opportunity description.
Assignments may shift throughout the event, so thank you in advance for bringing a flexible, positive attitude.
Please plan to stay for your entire shift. If you’d like to help but cannot stay for the full shift, email volunteer@a2gov.org so we can coordinate.
Arrival and Check-In
All volunteers will check in at the Gallup Park Meeting Room.
Please plan to arrive at least 15 minutes before your shift begins. Parking can be challenging during this popular event, and the parking area is about a 5–10 minute walk from volunteer check-in. Allowing extra time will help ensure you’re checked in and ready when your shift begins.
Find Your Role
Browse the calendar below to choose your station and shift.
Questions? Contact volunteer@a2gov.org or 734.794.6445.

title: Gardening at Bryant Community Center
description:
Show some love to Bryant Community Center! Join the Ann Arbor Parks Volunteer Program for a gardening workday focused on caring for the planted areas around this important neighborhood space.
Bryant Park and Community Center is located on the city’s south side and is home to the CAN Bryant Community Center. The park includes amenities such as a playground, walking trails, and a pavilion, making it a busy place for recreation, gathering, and community connection. 
During this event, volunteers will help weed garden beds, cut back shrubs, trim back grasses, and spread mulch. Weeds are taking over in some areas, and volunteers will help clear space so the beautiful plantings can continue to shine.
This work helps keep the community center grounds cared for, welcoming, and easier to maintain throughout the summer season. No prior gardening experience is necessary — staff will provide tools, supplies, training, and guidance on site.
Please note that the work areas may be hot and sunny. Volunteers should bring water and dress for the weather.
Come lend a hand and help spruce up Bryant Community Center!
Event Details:
  • Date: Thursday, October 15, 2026
  • Time: 10:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
  • Location: Bryant Community Center, 3 W Eden Ct, Ann Arbor
Volunteer tasks may include:
  • Weeding garden beds
  • Removing bedstraw from planted areas
  • Cutting back shrubs
  • Cutting back ornamental grasses
  • Light garden cleanup and beautification
What to wear and bring:
  • Comfortable clothing suitable for outdoor gardening
  • Long pants, tall socks, and closed-toe shoes
  • Dress for hot, sunny weather
  • A reusable water bottle
  • We provide all necessary tools and supplies
Please note:
  • This event may involve working in full sun
  • Tasks may involve bending, kneeling, clipping, or working close to the ground
  • Work areas may have uneven terrain or minor tripping hazards
  • All minors under 14 must be accompanied by a guardian

title: Monthly Clothing Swap
venue: Larcom City Hall, City Council Chambers, 2nd Floor
description:
​Join our monthly A²ZERO clothing swaps on the third Thursday of each month! Swaps are an opportunity to refresh your wardrobe, without buying new. Swaps are also a chance to gift your gently used clothes to members of your community, without contributing to the 92 million tons of textile waste generated globally each year. These are completely free events.  
​​​How it works: Each person can bring up to 10 items of clothing in good condition (no rips, holes, stains or unwashed items please!). Accessories such as bags, jewelry, and belts are also welcome. You can take clothing without bringing anything, or bring clothing without taking anything.  
​​​Skill Building Workshop: Stay tuned for more information!

title: Bluffs Nature Area - Invasive Shrub Cutting
description:
As caretakers of Ann Arbor’s Natural Areas, volunteers with the Ann Arbor Parks Department serve the greater community by:
  • Restoring local ecosystems
  • Expanding access to quality experiences in nature
  • Strengthening bonds through service
At this event, you’ll help protect Ann Arbor’s biodiversity and public lands by cutting and removing invasive shrubs with hand saws and loppers. This work creates more space for native plants to thrive, providing food and habitat for birds, pollinators, and other wildlife.
Event Details
  • Date: Sunday, October 18 2026
  • Time: 1:00 p.m.–4:00 p.m.
  • Location: Bluffs Nature Area 
  • Meeting Point: Meet at the park entrance on Sunset
    • Parking: There is street parking in the surrounding neighborhoods. We encourage carpooling and using public transportation, whenever possible.
What You’ll Be Doing
  • Using hand saws and loppers to cut invasive shrubs
  • Hauling brush and working off-trail
  • Supporting the long-term health of this natural area
Hazards & Safety Notes
This work involves the usual hazards of being in nature, including:
  • Off-trail walking on uneven surfaces and difficult footing
  • Exposure to plants with thorns and poison ivy
  • Muddy and hot conditions, depending on weather
  • Expect to get dirty while working outdoors
  • All minors must be accompanied by a gaurdian
What to Bring
  • Thick, long pants to protect against ticks and thorny plants
  • Closed-toe shoes (sturdy boots recommended)
  • Dress for the weather, likely hot and sunny, sun protection recommended
  • Filled water bottle
We Provide
  • Tools (hand saws, loppers), gloves, and training
  • Guidance from experienced staff
  • A chance to enjoy time in nature while giving back to your community
 More information: How to prepare for a NAP workday (PDF).

title: Ann Arbor Farmers Market Saturday Market Regular Hours
Mary Beth Doyle - Invasive Shrub Cutting
description:
As caretakers of Ann Arbor’s Natural Areas, volunteers with the Ann Arbor Parks Department serve the greater community by:
  • Restoring local ecosystems
  • Expanding access to quality experiences in nature
  • Strengthening bonds through service
At this event, you’ll help protect Ann Arbor’s biodiversity and public lands by cutting and removing invasive shrubs with hand saws and loppers. This work creates more space for native plants to thrive, providing food and habitat for birds, pollinators, and other wildlife.
Event Details
  • Date: Sunday, November 8, 2026
  • Time: 9:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
  • Location: Mary Beth Doyle Park
  • Meeting Point: Natural area entrance on east side of Mary Beth Doyle Park (intersection of Cardinal Ave & Sharon Dr)
    • Parking: There is street parking in the surrounding neighborhood. We encourage carpooling and using public transportation, whenever possible
What You’ll Be Doing
  • Using hand saws and loppers to cut invasive shrubs
  • Hauling brush and working off-trail
  • Supporting the long-term health of this natural area
Hazards & Safety Notes
This work involves the usual hazards of being in nature, including:
  • Off-trail walking on uneven surfaces and difficult footing
  • Exposure to plants with thorns and poison ivy
  • Expect to get dirty while working outdoors
  • All minors must be accompanied by a guardian
What to Bring
  • Thick, long pants to protect against ticks and thorny plants
  • Closed-toe shoes (sturdy boots recommended)
  • Dress for the weather
  • Filled water bottle
We Provide
  • Tools (hand saws, loppers), gloves, and training
  • Guidance from experienced staff
  • A chance to enjoy time in nature while giving back to your community
 More information: How to prepare for a NAP workday (PDF).
